minor.issue: Response includes the field name 'password_hash' as an empty string ('') for every client. The MongoDB projection correctly excludes the actual hash value, but because `Client` Pydantic model has `password_hash: Optional[str] = ''` and is used as `response_model=Client`, FastAPI re-materialises the field with its default empty string in the JSON response. Spec (Fase 6) requires 'password_hash never returned in any /api/clients response'. Recommended fix: either (a) remove `password_hash` from the `Client` response model (keep it only on a separate internal DB model / dict), or (b) add `response_model_exclude={'password_hash'}` to the two @api_router.get endpoints, or (c) return `_public_client(doc)` (same helper already used by portal endpoints) instead of relying on projection + response_model.

action_items: Fix password_hash leak in /api/clients list + detail (see backend_issues.minor). Value is always empty string so no actual hash exposed, but the field name shows up in responses which violates the Fase 6 spec ('password_hash never returned in any /api/clients response'). Suggested one-liner: return `_public_client(doc)` (already defined at server.py:1234) for both endpoints and drop `response_model=Client`, or remove password_hash from the Client Pydantic model.
(Carry-over from iter 5) Split server.py (~1360 lines) into routers/ (portal, clients, quotes, contracts, invoices, galleries, ai, public, settings) + models.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:84 — `Client` Pydantic model still declares `password_hash: Optional[str] = ''`. This is BOTH the DB representation AND the response_model for /api/clients. Because of that, the field always leaks into API responses as an empty string. Better pattern: keep password_hash only on the DB doc (raw dict) and define a separate `ClientPublic` response model without password_hash. The portal helper `_public_client()` already exists and does exactly this pop — use it for /api/clients too.

server.py:1241 `get_current_client` — the Bearer token dependency is fine (matches playbook fallback pattern). Consider caching the client lookup or moving to a small `get_current_client_cached` if latency becomes an issue; currently every portal request does one extra Mongo find_one.

server.py:1258 portal_login — uses a case-insensitive regex to match email. Regex is built from user input (`payload.email`) with `$regex: f'^{email}$'`. If the email contains regex metacharacters (e.g. `.` or `+`), the match still works (dots and pluses are harmless), but a malicious email with `.*` could theoretically match multiple docs. Recommend `re.escape(email)` or just do `{'email': email}` with a case-insensitive collation, or store emails already lowercased and do exact match on the pre-lowercased value.
server.py:1257 login — no rate-limiting / brute-force protection. Spec doesn't require it for Fase 6 MVP, but is a known gap for future hardening.

server.py:1272 forgot-password — stores reset tokens in `db.password_reset_tokens` but no endpoint exists yet to consume them (POST /reset). Mocked as spec allows (logs to console). Documented, not a bug.

portalAuth.jsx:22 — on token-in-storage but /me returns 401 (expired/invalid), the code removes the token but leaves `client=null` and `ready=true`; PortalLayout then correctly redirects to /portal/login. Good.

PortalPages.jsx PortalProfile — uses `form.tax_id || form.nif` as the initial value for the tax input, gracefully bridging the legacy `nif` field and the new i18n `tax_id`. Nice touch; consistent with the Clients page workaround from iter 5.

PortalPages.jsx PortalDashboard uses `eur()` from lib/api for both KPI values. This will follow the same i18n-currency behavior as the photographer app (currency comes from Definições). Verified: 'Por pagar 3936,00 €' rendered in PT default.

App.js — PortalAuthProvider is wrapped around each /portal route separately (line 48 vs 49). This means the /portal/login route uses a DIFFERENT PortalAuthProvider instance than the /portal/* routes. Practical effect: after login on /portal/login, the token is persisted to localStorage but the /portal PortalAuthProvider instance re-reads it on mount and calls /me. This works but adds an extra round-trip on every login→dashboard transition (visible in DevTools). Consider lifting a single PortalAuthProvider above both Routes, or making the /portal/login route a child of the /portal layout with its own bypass logic.

SettingsProvider wraps the entire app INCLUDING /portal/login. Portal login therefore blocks on the /api/settings GET before rendering. Minor: portal login could technically render without settings. Not blocking.

rca of the issue: password_hash leak RCA: server.py Client Pydantic model (line 84) declares password_hash as a serializable field with default ''. The two GET /api/clients endpoints use response_model=Client so FastAPI serialises the Pydantic model — filling missing fields (password_hash was projected out by Mongo) with their default value. Reproduction: `curl {BASE}/api/clients | jq '.[0].password_hash'` returns `""`. Mitigation: change return statement to `return [_public_client(d) for d in await db.clients.find(...).to_list(1000)]` and drop `response_model=Client` (or add response_model_exclude={'password_hash'}). Portal endpoints already do this correctly.
